stem: Inherent goodwill is best described as goodwill:

options.content: that the business has built up itself and has not been bought
options.rationale: Correct: it is self-generated through reputation and customers.

options.content: paid for when one business buys another
options.rationale: That describes purchased goodwill.

options.content: calculated as the difference between assets and liabilities
options.rationale: That is net assets or capital.

options.content: that is shown as a non-current asset in the statement of financial position
options.rationale: Inherent goodwill is not recognised.

explanation: Inherent goodwill arises from the business's own reputation and is not recorded in the books.

stem: Why is a goodwill account usually eliminated immediately after it is created on a change in a partnership?

options.content: Inherent goodwill cannot be recognised as an asset
options.rationale: Correct: IAS 38 does not allow self-generated goodwill to be shown.

options.content: Goodwill has no value to the partners
options.rationale: It has value, which is why it is shared between the partners.

options.content: The new partner does not want to pay for it
options.rationale: The elimination charges the continuing partners in the new ratio.

options.content: Goodwill is always replaced by cash
options.rationale: No cash need be involved.

explanation: Because inherent goodwill is not an asset the business can recognise, the account is opened only to adjust the partners' capital.

stem: A partnership's profits for the last three years were US\$18,200, US\$21,400 and US\$22,800. Goodwill is valued at two years' purchase of average profits. What is the value of goodwill?

options.rationale: The total of the profits has been used, not the average.
Correct: average 20,800 × 2.
The multiple of two years has been left out.
Only the latest year's profit has been used.

stem: Partners share profits 3 : 2 and will share 1 : 1. What is the sacrifice of the partner with the 3/5 share?

options.rationale: The shares have been compared by a different method; the difference is 1/10.
That is half of 3/5 and not a difference.

options.content: No sacrifice; the partner gains
options.rationale: The share falls from 0.6 to 0.5.

explanation: 3/5 = 6/10 and 1/2 = 5/10, so the sacrifice is 1/10.

stem: When goodwill is created on a change in profit-sharing, which entry is made?

options.content: Debit goodwill; credit the new partners' capital accounts in the new ratio
options.rationale: Goodwill is created for the old partners in the old ratio.

options.content: Debit the old partners' capital accounts; credit goodwill
options.rationale: That is the opposite entry, a write-off.

options.content: Debit goodwill; credit the old partners' capital accounts in the old ratio
options.rationale: Correct: the old partners built the goodwill.

options.content: Debit cash; credit goodwill
options.rationale: Goodwill does not involve cash unless a premium is paid.

explanation: The old partners are credited with the value they created, in the ratio in which they shared profits.

stem: Goodwill is eliminated from the books when the new profit-sharing ratio starts. Which entry is made?

options.content: Debit the partners' capital accounts in the old ratio; credit goodwill
options.rationale: The elimination uses the new ratio.

options.content: Credit the partners' capital accounts in the new ratio; debit goodwill
options.rationale: That repeats the creation.

options.content: Debit goodwill; credit profit and loss
options.rationale: No profit is involved.

options.content: Debit the partners' capital accounts in the new ratio; credit goodwill
options.rationale: Correct: the new partners bear the cost in the new ratio.

explanation: The partners who will share profits in the new ratio are charged with the goodwill.
hints: Who will share future profits and so benefit?

stem: No goodwill account is opened. Goodwill is US\$60,000, and partner X gains 1/10 of the profit share while partner Y sacrifices 1/10. Which adjustment is made to the capital accounts?

options.content: Debit Y US\$6,000; credit X US\$6,000
options.rationale: The adjustment is reversed.

options.content: Debit X US\$60,000; credit Y US\$60,000
options.rationale: The whole goodwill has been used rather than the 1/10 share.

options.content: Debit X US\$600; credit Y US\$600
options.rationale: The figure has been mis-scaled by a factor of ten.

options.content: Debit X US\$6,000; credit Y US\$6,000
options.rationale: Correct: the gaining partner pays the sacrificing partner 1/10 of the goodwill.

explanation: 1/10 × 60,000 = 6,000 is transferred from the gaining partner's capital to the sacrificing partner's capital.

stem: Average annual profit is US\$31,500. Net assets are US\$150,000 and a normal return is 12% of net assets. Goodwill is three years' purchase of super profits. What is its value?

options.rationale: The normal return has not been deducted.
The multiple of three years has been left out.
The normal return alone has been multiplied.

explanation: Normal return 18,000; super profits 13,500; goodwill 13,500 × 3 = 40,500.

stem: Under IAS 38 inherent goodwill may be recorded as an asset if the partners agree its value.
explanation: False. Self-generated goodwill cannot be reliably measured and is not recognised, whatever the partners agree.

stem: The sacrifices and gains of all the partners in a change of ratio add up to zero.
explanation: True. Total profit shares are 1 before and after, so what one partner loses another gains.
hints: Total shares before and after are both 1.

stem: Match each term to its description.

right.content: Built up by the business and not recorded
Paid for on acquiring a business
Average profit above the normal return on net assets
Old profit share less new profit share

explanation: Inherent goodwill is self-built; purchased goodwill is paid for; super profits exceed the normal return; sacrifice is old share less new share.

stem: Complete the entries when goodwill is created.

payload.template: Debit {{blank:a}}; credit the {{blank:b}} partners' capital accounts in the {{blank:c}} ratio.

explanation: Goodwill is created for the old partners in the old ratio.

stem: Name the ratio found by subtracting each partner's new profit share from the old share.
explanation: A positive result is the sacrifice; a negative result is a gain.

stem: Chipo and Nyasha share profits 5 : 3 and will share equally. Goodwill is valued at US\$36,000 and no goodwill account is to be kept. Calculate the amount transferred from Nyasha's capital account to Chipo's capital account.
explanation: Chipo's share falls from 5/8 to 1/2 (sacrifice 1/8) and Nyasha's rises from 3/8 to 1/2 (gain 1/8). Transfer = 1/8 × 36,000 = 4,500. Wrongly using half the goodwill gives 18,000.
workedSolution: 1. Chipo's share falls from 5/8 to 1/2 (sacrifice 1/8) and Nyasha's rises from 3/8 to 1/2 (gain 1/8). Transfer = 1/8 × 36,000 = 4,500. Wrongly using half the goodwill gives 18,000.

stem: The average annual profit of a partnership is US\$26,800. Its net assets are US\$94,000 and the normal rate of return is 14%. Goodwill is valued at four years' purchase of super profits. Calculate the value of goodwill.

Nyasha and Farai share profits 2 : 1. They admit Sipho and will share profits 3 : 3 : 2 (Nyasha : Farai : Sipho). Goodwill is US\$48,000 and is eliminated. Calculate the amount of goodwill charged to Sipho's capital account.
explanation: Sipho's share is 2/8 = 1/4. Charged = 1/4 × 48,000 = 12,000. (Nyasha 3/8 and Farai 3/8 are charged 18,000 each; the old partners are credited 32,000 and 16,000.)
workedSolution: 1. Sipho's share is 2/8 = 1/4. Charged = 1/4 × 48,000 = 12,000. (Nyasha 3/8 and Farai 3/8 are charged 18,000 each; the old partners are credited 32,000 and 16,000.)

stem: State two reasons why a business may have goodwill.

points.description: A favourable location, skilled staff or exclusive supply agreements

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A strong reputation and loyal customers, and a good location or skilled employees.

explanation: One mark for each reason.

stem: Explain why the old partners are credited with goodwill when a new partner is admitted.

points.description: The goodwill was built up by the old partners over the years
The new partner will share in future profits that the goodwill helps to earn
Crediting the old partners compensates them for the share of future profit they give up

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The old partners built the business's reputation. The new partner will share in future profits that depend on it, so the old partners are credited to compensate them for giving up part of those profits.

explanation: One mark for each of the three points.
hints: Who built the goodwill, and who benefits afterwards?

stem: The partners cannot agree whether to value goodwill using average profits or super profits. Evaluate the two methods.

points.description: The average profits method is simple and easy to agree but ignores the capital employed in earning the profit
The super profits method deducts a normal return on net assets, so it values only the profit due to reputation; it is more precise but depends on the chosen normal rate and years' purchase
Both depend on judgement of the years' purchase and on whether past profits will continue
Judgement: super profits are fairer for a capital-heavy business; average profits may suit a service business with few assets

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Average profits is simple but ignores the capital used to earn the profit. Super profits gives a fairer picture of the profit due to reputation but relies on the normal rate chosen. Both rely on judgement of the number of years. For a capital-heavy business super profits is fairer.

explanation: One mark for each method, one for the shared weakness and one for a judgement.
hints: Which method takes account of assets?
